co_ice_caves_the.blurb: The Ice Caves are a set of water-carved granite caves and slots near the Grottos day-use area on the Independence Pass road east of Aspen. The twelve climbs here are mostly boulder problems plus a few trad lines. The bouldering is hard, running from V6 up into the low teens, with only a handful of problems in the middle grades. Expect steep, overhanging rock with small holds and little for the feet, so it suits strong climbers more than newcomers. A short walk from the day-use area leads to the caves, and you will want pads.

co_peter_wall.blurb: Peter Wall is a small roadside cliff in Unaweep Canyon, part of the Nine Mile Hill roped climbing zone outside Grand Junction. Twelve routes are listed, almost all of them traditional lines with a single sport route, and the grades cluster around 5.10 with a few at 5.9 and a couple of 5.11s. It is the busiest wall of the zone by route count, though still a modest crag, and a good pick for a mid-grade trad day when you want a short outing. The face catches sun through the early afternoon and then falls into shade, which makes it workable on warmer days.

co_obscura.blurb: Obscura is the largest of the little crags in the Lilliput group east of Buena Vista, on the slope above a dirt county road near Trout Creek Pass. It holds twelve routes of an easy to moderate kind: mostly traditional lines, four bolted routes and a single top-rope, with grades running from the low 5th class up through 5.9 and the bulk around 5.7 to 5.8. The wall faces west, so afternoons are warm and mornings cool. The short uphill walk, modest height and gentle grades make it a relaxed stop for newer leaders.

co_hotdish_rock.blurb: Hotdish Rock is one tall boulder in the Boondocks section of the Blue Moon bouldering zone, tucked at the base of the west wall of Unaweep Canyon near Grand Junction. All four faces carry problems, twelve in total, and they run from V1 to V4 with most at V2 and V3, which makes it a friendly block for people building up to harder grades. Landings are mostly flat and clear and the rock is solid. Because the boulder is tall, there is an easy hop-off at the northeast corner. The Boondocks tend to be in shade by late afternoon, so it holds up in warm weather.

co_juniper_wall.blurb: Juniper Wall is a trad crag on the granite of the main Unaweep Canyon, the first big granite face a driver meets on the left when heading up the canyon from the west. About a dozen routes are recorded, all traditional, ranging from the 5.8 range to the low 5.12s, with a stack of them at 5.10 to 5.12. The climbing is on the hard side for a first visit, and the canyon's rock can be complex and sometimes loose or blocky. The wall is considered less rewarding than the canyon's classic walls, so it fits climbers already comfortable on technical crack and face routes.

co_funny_face_the.blurb: The Funny Face is a compact, closely bolted sport wall in the Ice Cave Walls sector of Rifle Mountain Park, reached by a short creekside trail from the middle parking lot. Its twelve routes are all sport, mostly 5.9 to 5.11 with five at 5.10 and one at 5.12, so it suits climbers aiming for the 5.10 and 5.11 range. The wall looks west across the canyon, so it gets morning sun and afternoon shade. Seeps can wet the rock in spring, and polish on the popular lines is worth knowing about.

co_first_overhang.blurb: First Overhang is a roadside boulder on Flagstaff Mountain above Boulder, with its namesake overhanging classic and a cluster of variations around it. The twelve problems range from V2 through V8, most from V4 to V8, including sit starts and traverses of the main line. The problems sit on the south face, which makes the spot a good midday option in cold months and a morning or evening one when it is hot. It is a quick stop from the car rather than a full day. Bring pads.
